method.paper: PubMed record indexed Humans[MeSH] that matches the human pancreas query and is annotated by PubTator3 with the human gene (NCBI Gene ID)
method.scope: human pancreatic cancer papers: human pancreas papers that are pancreatic cancer papers (all human pancreas papers minus those left after excluding pancreatic cancer)
method.cellTypePaper: scope paper that also matches the PubMed query of the cell type (MeSH and title/abstract terms)
method.expected: scope papers x cellTypeShare; cellTypeShare = share of gene-annotated scope papers that match the cell-type query
method.enrichment: (observed + 0.5) / (expected + 0.5); expected and enrichment rounded to 3 decimals
method.union: a gene set is counted on the union of its member genes' papers, each paper once
method.recent: newest publication year first, then higher PMID
method.caution: Counts measure research attention. Gene annotations are automatic and gene names can be ambiguous; a paper that mentions a gene and a cell type is not evidence that the gene acts in that cell type.

fields.cellTypes: cell type -> record, in the order of meta.cellTypes
fields.scopePapers: human pancreatic cancer papers in PubMed that match the cell-type query
fields.scopePapersGeneAnnotated: those with at least one gene annotation of any species (the papers behind cellTypeShare)
fields.scopePapersWithHumanGene: those annotated with at least one human gene
fields.share: scopePapersGeneAnnotated of the cell type / scopePapersGeneAnnotated of the whole scope; multiplies a gene's scope papers to give its expected count
fields.genesObserved: human genes with at least 1 scope paper in the cell type
fields.genesEligible: human genes with at least 5 scope papers in the cell type
fields.topGenes: up to 50 eligible genes with the highest enrichment (ties: more observed papers, then symbol): [gene, observed, expected, enrichment, scopePapers of the gene, up to 3 most recent PMIDs in the cell type]
fields.titles: PMID -> {t: title, j: journal abbreviation, y: publication year} for every PMID in topGenes
